newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian capital hit by new mystery bombings.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian capital hit by new mystery bombings.

text.p: Two hand grenades blew up in Budapest early on Monday, damaging two shops, in the latest of a rash of mystery bombings in Hungary.
Police said the two grenades exploded at about 1:30 a.m. in a commercial section of the city, blowing out the windows of a car showroom and a small restaurant. There were no injuries.
National police spokesman Laszlo Garamvolgyi declined to speculate on the reasons for the bombings.
Hungary has been hit by a rash of bombings this year, including another over the weekend in which a hand grenade damaged a luxury car in Budapest.

The car, heavily damaged early on Saturday, belonged to a games arcade and gambling machine operator, the national news agency MTI said. Police said the bomb had probably been planted by his business rivals to intimidate him.
Earlier this month a small bomb exploded in a dustbin near Budapest's Dohanyi Utca Synagogue, Europe's largest synagogue. Noone was injured.
As of mid-October, the Hungarian press reported that police were investigating 13 explosions of grenades and other devices this year, compared to 28 blasts in the preceding seven years.
Police have said that most bombings in Hungary are linked to criminal attacks or suicide attempts. They say they have no evidence of terrorist groups operating in the country.
